sanskrit: atha satyavatī garbhaṃ kṣatriyāntakaraṃ tadā dhārayām āsa dīptena vapuṣā ghoradarśanam
english: Then Satyavatī bore in her womb the embryo destined to be the destroyer of the Kṣatriyas, of blazing form and terrible to behold.

sanskrit: tām ṛcīkas tadā dṛṣṭvā dhyānayogena vai tataḥ abravīd rājaśārdūla svāṃ bhāryāṃ varavarṇinīm
english: Seeing her thus, Ṛcīka, perceiving the matter by the power of meditation, then spoke to his fair-complexioned wife, O tiger among kings.

sanskrit: mātrāsi vyaṃsitā bhadre caruvyatyāsahetunā janiṣyate hi te putraḥ krūrakarmā mahābalaḥ
english: "You have been deceived by your mother, gentle lady, through the exchange of the sacrificial offerings; for now a son of cruel deeds and mighty strength shall be born to you.

sanskrit: janiṣyate hi te bhrātā brahmabhūtas tapodhanaḥ viśvaṃ hi brahma tapasā mayā tatra samarpitam
english: And a brother shall be born to you who is the very embodiment of Brahman, rich in austerity; for through my penance I infused into that offering the whole power of the sacred word."

sanskrit: saivam uktā mahābhāgā bhartrā satyavatī tadā papāta śirasā tasmai vepantī cābravīd idam
english: Thus addressed by her husband, the blessed Satyavatī then fell at his feet with her head bowed and, trembling, spoke these words:

sanskrit: nārho 'si bhagavann adya vaktum evaṃvidhaṃ vacaḥ brāhmaṇāpasadaṃ putraṃ prāpsyasīti mahāmune
english: "You ought not, O blessed one, to utter today such words as these—'You shall obtain a son who is a degenerate among Brahmins,' O great sage."

sanskrit: ṛcīka uvāca naiṣa saṃkalpitaḥ kāmo mayā bhadre tathā tvayi ugrakarmā bhavet putraś carur mātā ca kāraṇam
english: Ṛcīka said: "This was not the wish I intended in your case, gentle lady; that your son should be of fierce deeds—the cause of this is the offering and your mother."

sanskrit: satyavaty uvāca icchaṃl lokān api mune sṛjethāḥ kiṃ punar mama śamātmakam ṛjuṃ putraṃ labheyaṃ japatāṃ vara
english: Satyavatī said: "Were you to wish it, O sage, you could create whole worlds; how much more easily then could I, through you, obtain a son who is peaceable in spirit and upright, O best of those who recite the sacred prayers."

sanskrit: ṛcīka uvāca noktapūrvaṃ mayā bhadre svaireṣv apy anṛtaṃ vacaḥ kim utāgniṃ samādhāya mantravac carusādhane
english: Ṛcīka said: "Never before, gentle lady, have I spoken a false word even in jest—how much less when I have kindled the fire and prepared the offering with sacred mantras.

sanskrit: satyavaty uvāca kāmam evaṃ bhavet pautro mameha tava caiva ha śamātmakam ṛjuṃ putraṃ labheyaṃ japatāṃ vara
english: Satyavatī said: "Let it be, then, that such a one shall be my grandson—and yours as well; but may I obtain a son who is peaceable in spirit and upright, O best of those who recite the sacred prayers."

sanskrit: ṛcīka uvāca putre nāsti viśeṣo me pautre vā varavarṇini yathā tvayoktaṃ tu vacas tathā bhadre bhaviṣyati
english: Ṛcīka said: "To me there is no difference between son and grandson, O fair-complexioned one; even as you have spoken, gentle lady, so shall it come to pass."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tataḥ satyavatī putraṃ janayām āsa bhārgavam tapasy abhirataṃ śāntaṃ jamadagniṃ śamātmakam
english: Vāsudeva said: Then Satyavatī gave birth to a son of the line of Bhṛgu—Jamadagni, devoted to austerity, tranquil, and peaceable in spirit.

sanskrit: viśvāmitraṃ ca dāyādaṃ gādhiḥ kuśikanandanaḥ prāpa brahmarṣisamitaṃ viśvena brahmaṇā yutam
english: And Gādhi, son of Kuśika, obtained as his heir Viśvāmitra, equal to the Brahmin sages and endowed with the whole power of the sacred word.

sanskrit: ārcīko janayām āsa jamadagniḥ sudāruṇam sarvavidyāntagaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanurvede ca pāragam rāmaṃ kṣatriyahantāraṃ pradīptam iva pāvakam
english: Jamadagni, son of Ṛcīka, begot the most terrible Rāma—master of every branch of learning, supreme, accomplished in the science of archery, the slayer of the Kṣatriyas, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu kṛtavīryātmajo balī arjuno nāma tejasvī kṣatriyo haihayānvayaḥ
english: Now at that very time there lived the mighty son of Kṛtavīrya, Arjuna by name, a lustrous Kṣatriya of the lineage of the Haihayas.

sanskrit: dadāha pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ saptadvīpāṃ sapattanām svabāhvastrabalenājau dharmeṇa parameṇa ca
english: He ruled the whole earth with its seven continents and its cities by the strength of his own arms and weapons in battle, and by the highest righteousness.

sanskrit: tṛṣitena sa kauravya bhikṣitaś citrabhānunā sahasrabāhur vikrāntaḥ prādād bhikṣām athāgnaye
english: O Kaurava, when he was begged by the hungry Citrabhānu—the Fire—that valiant one of a thousand arms granted alms to Agni.

sanskrit: grāmān purāṇi ghoṣāṃś ca pattanāni ca vīryavān jajvāla tasya bāṇais tu citrabhānur didhakṣayā
english: With his arrows the valiant king set ablaze villages, towns, cowherds' settlements, and cities, for Citrabhānu was eager to consume them in flame.

sanskrit: sa tasya puruṣendrasya prabhāvena mahātapāḥ dadāha kārtavīryasya śailān atha vanāni ca
english: Through the power of that lord among men, Kārtavīrya, the great-glowing Fire burned the mountains and forests as well.

sanskrit: sa śūnyam āśramāraṇyaṃ varuṇasyātmajasya tat dadāha pavaneneddhaś citrabhānuḥ sahaihayaḥ
english: Fanned by the wind, Citrabhānu, together with the Haihaya, burned the deserted forest hermitage of the son of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: āpavas taṃ tato roṣāc chaśāpārjunam acyuta dagdhe ''śrame mahārāja kārtavīryeṇa vīryavān
english: Then, O unfallen one, when his hermitage had been burned by Kārtavīrya, the valiant sage Āpava in his wrath cursed Arjuna, O great king:

sanskrit: tvayā na varjitaṃ mohād yasmād vanam idaṃ mama dagdhaṃ tasmād raṇe rāmo bāhūṃs te chetsyate 'rjuna
english: "Because in your folly you did not spare this forest of mine but let it be burned, therefore in battle, O Arjuna, Rāma shall sever your arms."

sanskrit: arjunas tu mahārāja balī nityaṃ śamātmakaḥ brahmaṇyaś ca śaraṇyaś ca dātā śūraś ca bhārata
english: Yet Arjuna, O great king, was mighty, ever peaceable in spirit, devoted to the Brahmins, a refuge to those who sought it, generous, and heroic, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tasya putrāḥ subalinaḥ śāpenāsan pitur vadhe nimittam avaliptā vai nṛśaṃsāś caiva nityadā
english: His sons were exceedingly strong, but through the curse they became the instruments of their father's slaying—arrogant they were, and cruel at all times.

sanskrit: jamadagnidhenvās te vatsam āninyur bharatarṣabha ajñātaṃ kārtavīryasya haihayendrasya dhīmataḥ
english: They carried off the calf of Jamadagni's cow, O bull of the Bharatas, without the knowledge of the wise Kārtavīrya, lord of the Haihayas.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunasya bāhūṃs tu chittvā vai pauruṣānvitaḥ taṃ ruvantaṃ tato vatsaṃ jāmadagnyaḥ svam āśramam pratyānayata rājendra teṣām antaḥpurāt prabhuḥ
english: Then the son of Jamadagni, endowed with manly valor, severed the arms of Arjuna and brought back to his own hermitage the lowing calf from their inner apartments, O lord of kings, that mighty lord.

sanskrit: arjunasya sutās te tu saṃbhūyābuddhayas tadā gatvāśramam asaṃbuddhaṃ jamadagner mahātmanaḥ
english: But those witless sons of Arjuna then banded together and went, unannounced, to the hermitage of the great-souled Jamadagni.

sanskrit: apātayanta bhallāgraiḥ śiraḥ kāyān narādhipa samitkuśārthaṃ rāmasya nirgatasya mahātmanaḥ
english: With their broad-headed arrows they struck off his head from his body, O ruler of men, while the great-souled Rāma had gone out to gather firewood and kuśa grass.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitṛvadhāmarṣād rāmaḥ paramamanyumān niḥkṣatriyāṃ pratiśrutya mahīṃ śastram agṛhṇata
english: Then, in his fury at his father's murder, Rāma, filled with utmost wrath, vowed to rid the earth of Kṣatriyas and took up his weapon.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhṛguśārdūlaḥ kārtavīryasya vīryavān vikramya nijaghānāśu putrān pautrāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then that tiger of the Bhṛgus, the valiant one, advancing in his might, swiftly slew the sons and grandsons of Kārtavīrya, every one of them.

sanskrit: sa haihayasahasrāṇi hatvā paramamanyumān cakāra bhārgavo rājan mahīṃ śoṇitakardamām
english: Having slain thousands of Haihayas, the descendant of Bhṛgu, filled with utmost wrath, made the earth into a mire of blood, O king.

sanskrit: sa tathā sumahātejāḥ kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṃ mahīm kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo vanam eva jagāma ha
english: Having thus rid the earth of Kṣatriyas, that one of vast splendor, overcome by deep compassion, withdrew into the forest.

sanskrit: tato varṣasahasreṣu samatīteṣu keṣu cit kṣobhaṃ saṃprāptavāṃs tīvraṃ prakṛtyā kopanaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Then, after some thousands of years had passed, that lord, irascible by nature, was driven to fierce agitation.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrasya pautras tu raibhyaputro mahātapāḥ parāvasur mahārāja kṣiptvāha janasaṃsadi
english: For the grandson of Viśvāmitra, son of Raibhya, the great ascetic Parāvasu, O great king, taunted him and said in the assembly of men:

sanskrit: ye te yayātipatane yajñe santaḥ samāgatāḥ pratardanaprabhṛtayo rāma kiṃ kṣatriyā na te
english: "Those worthy men who gathered at the sacrifice held at the fall of Yayāti—Pratardana and the rest—were they not Kṣatriyas, O Rāma?

sanskrit: mithyāpratijño rāma tvaṃ katthase janasaṃsadi bhayāt kṣatriyavīrāṇāṃ parvataṃ samupāśritaḥ
english: False to your vow are you, O Rāma; you boast in the assembly of men, yet out of fear of the Kṣatriya heroes you have taken refuge in the mountain."

sanskrit: sa punaḥ kṣatriyaśataiḥ pṛthivīm anusaṃtatām parāvasos tadā śrutvā śastraṃ jagrāha bhārgavaḥ
english: Hearing then these words of Parāvasu, the descendant of Bhṛgu, seeing the earth once more thickly peopled with hundreds of Kṣatriyas, took up his weapon again.

sanskrit: tato ye kṣatriyā rājañ śataśas tena jīvitāḥ te vivṛddhā mahāvīryāḥ pṛthivīpatayo 'bhavan
english: Then those Kṣatriyas, O king, who in their hundreds had been spared by him, had grown up and become mighty lords of the earth.

sanskrit: sa punas tāñ jaghānāśu bālān api narādhipa garbhasthais tu mahī vyāptā punar evābhavat tadā
english: He swiftly slew them again, O ruler of men, even the very children; yet once more the earth was filled with those still in the womb.

sanskrit: jātaṃ jātaṃ sa garbhaṃ tu punar eva jaghāna ha arakṣaṃś ca sutān kāṃś cit tadā kṣatriyayoṣitaḥ
english: And each embryo, as soon as it was born, he slew again; yet the Kṣatriya women managed to save some of their sons.

sanskrit: triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivīṃ kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṃ prabhuḥ dakṣiṇām aśvamedhānte kaśyapāyādadat tataḥ
english: Thrice seven times that lord rid the earth of Kṣatriyas, and then, at the close of a horse-sacrifice, he gave it as the priestly fee to Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu śeṣārthaṃ kareṇoddiśya kaśyapaḥ srukpragrahavatā rājañ śrīmān vākyam athābravīt
english: Then, for the sake of the surviving Kṣatriyas, the illustrious Kaśyapa, pointing with the hand that held the sacrificial ladle, spoke these words, O king:

sanskrit: gaccha pāraṃ samudrasya dakṣiṇasya mahāmune na te madviṣaye rāma vastavyam iha karhi cit
english: "Go to the farther shore of the southern ocean, O great sage; never henceforth, O Rāma, may you dwell here within my domain."

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpārakaṃ deśaṃ sāgaras tasya nirmame saṃtrāsāj jāmadagnyasya so 'parāntaṃ mahītalam
english: Then, out of dread of the son of Jamadagni, the ocean fashioned for him the land of Śūrpāraka, that western tract of the earth.

sanskrit: kaśyapas tu mahārāja pratigṛhya mahīm imām kṛtvā brāhmaṇasaṃsthāṃ vai praviveśa mahāvanam
english: But Kaśyapa, O great king, having received this earth and placed it under the governance of the Brahmins, entered the great forest.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūdrāś ca vaiśyāś ca yathāsvairapracāriṇaḥ avartanta dvijāgryāṇāṃ dāreṣu bharatarṣabha
english: Then the Śūdras and the Vaiśyas, acting wantonly each as he pleased, behaved disgracefully toward the wives of the foremost of the twice-born, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: arājake jīvaloke durbalā balavattaraiḥ bādhyante na ca vitteṣu prabhutvam iha kasya cit
english: In a kingless world the weak are oppressed by the stronger, and no man here holds secure ownership over his wealth.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena pṛthivī praviveśa rasātalam arakṣyamāṇā vidhivat kṣatriyair dharmarakṣibhiḥ
english: Then in course of time the earth, no longer duly protected by Kṣatriyas who guard the law, began to sink into the nether regions.

sanskrit: ūruṇā dhārayām āsa kaśyapaḥ pṛthivīṃ tataḥ nimajjantīṃ tadā rājaṃs tenorvīti mahī smṛtā
english: Then Kaśyapa upheld upon his thigh the earth as she was sinking, O king; and from this, men say, the earth is called Urvī.

sanskrit: rakṣiṇaś ca samuddiśya prāyācat pṛthivī tadā prasādya kaśyapaṃ devī kṣatriyān bāhuśālinaḥ
english: Then the goddess Earth, having propitiated Kaśyapa, besought him, naming as her protectors the strong-armed Kṣatriyas:

sanskrit: santi brahman mayā guptā nṛṣu kṣatriyapuṃgavāḥ haihayānāṃ kule jātās te saṃrakṣantu māṃ mune
english: "There are, O Brahmin, certain bulls among Kṣatriyas, hidden by me among men, born in the lineage of the Haihayas; let these protect me, O sage.

sanskrit: asti pauravadāyādo viḍūrathasutaḥ prabho ṛkṣaiḥ saṃvardhito vipra ṛkṣavaty eva parvate
english: There is an heir of the Pauravas, the son of Viḍūratha, O lord, who was reared by bears upon the mountain Ṛkṣavat, O Brahmin.

sanskrit: tathānukampamānena yajvanāthāmitaujasā parāśareṇa dāyādaḥ saudāsasyābhirakṣitaḥ
english: So too the heir of Saudāsa was protected out of compassion by Parāśara, the sacrificer of immeasurable might.

sanskrit: sarvakarmāṇi kurute tasyarṣeḥ śūdravad dhi saḥ sarvakarmety abhikhyātaḥ sa māṃ rakṣatu pārthivaḥ
english: He performs all menial tasks for that sage like a Śūdra, and so is known as Sarvakarman, 'doer of every work'; let that prince protect me.

sanskrit: śibeḥ putro mahātejā gopatir nāma nāmataḥ vane saṃrakṣito gobhiḥ so 'bhirakṣatu māṃ mune
english: The son of Śibi, of great splendor, Gopati by name, was protected in the forest by cattle; let him protect me, O sage.

sanskrit: pratardanasya putras tu vatso nāma mahāyaśāḥ vatsaiḥ saṃvardhito goṣṭhe sa māṃ rakṣatu pārthivaḥ
english: The son of Pratardana, of great renown, Vatsa by name, was reared among the calves in the cow-pen; let that prince protect me.

sanskrit: dadhivāhanapautras tu putro divirathasya ha aṅgaḥ sa gautamenāpi gaṅgākūle 'bhirakṣitaḥ
english: And Aṅga, the grandson of Dadhivāhana and son of Diviratha, was likewise protected by Gautama upon the bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: bṛhadratho mahābāhur bhuvi bhūtipuraskṛtaḥ golāṅgūlair mahābhāgo gṛdhrakūṭe 'bhirakṣitaḥ
english: The mighty-armed Bṛhadratha, honored with prosperity upon the earth, that blessed one, was protected by black-tailed monkeys upon Gṛdhrakūṭa.

sanskrit: maruttasyānvavāye tu kṣatriyās turvasos trayaḥ marutpatisamā vīrye samudreṇābhirakṣitāḥ
english: And in the line of Marutta, three Kṣatriyas of Turvasu's race, equal in valor to the lord of the Maruts, were protected by the ocean.

sanskrit: ete kṣatriyadāyādās tatra tatra pariśrutāḥ samyaṅ mām abhirakṣantu tataḥ sthāsyāmi niścalā
english: These heirs of the Kṣatriyas, renowned here and there, let them duly protect me; then shall I stand firm and unshaken.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ pitaraś caiva tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ madarthaṃ nihatā yuddhe rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: The fathers of these men, and likewise their grandfathers, were slain in battle for my sake by Rāma of untiring deeds.

sanskrit: teṣām apacitiś caiva mayā kāryā na saṃśayaḥ na hy ahaṃ kāmaye nityam avikrāntena rakṣaṇam
english: To them too I must surely make requital; for I do not desire to be protected forever by one who is without valor.

sanskrit: tataḥ pṛthivyā nirdiṣṭāṃs tān samānīya kaśyapaḥ abhyaṣiñcan mahīpālān kṣatriyān vīryasaṃmatān
english: Then Kaśyapa gathered together those whom the Earth had named and consecrated them as guardians of the earth—Kṣatriyas esteemed for their valor.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca yeṣāṃ vaṃśāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ evam etat purā vṛttaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasi pāṇḍava
english: From their sons and grandsons the dynasties were established. Thus it was that this came to pass of old, concerning which you ask me, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bruvann eva yadupravīro; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham rathena tenāśu yayau yathārko; viśan prabhābhir bhagavāṃs trilokam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as he spoke thus, that foremost hero of the Yadus, addressing Yudhiṣṭhira, the best of the upholders of righteousness, swiftly drove on in that chariot, like the blessed Sun pervading the three worlds with his rays.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rāmasya tat karma śrutvā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā pratyuvāca janārdanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having heard of that deed of Rāma, King Yudhiṣṭhira, filled with the utmost wonder, replied to Janārdana:

sanskrit: aho rāmasya vārṣṇeya śakrasyeva mahātmanaḥ vikramo yena vasudhā krodhān niḥkṣatriyā kṛtā
english: "Ah, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, what valor was that of the great-souled Rāma, like to Śakra's, whereby in his wrath he rid the earth of Kṣatriyas!

sanskrit: gobhiḥ samudreṇa tathā golāṅgūlarkṣavānaraiḥ guptā rāmabhayodvignāḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ kulodvahāḥ
english: By cattle, by the ocean, and by black-tailed monkeys, bears, and apes were the bearers of the Kṣatriya lineages protected, trembling in fear of Rāma.

sanskrit: aho dhanyo hi loko 'yaṃ sabhāgyāś ca narā bhuvi yatra karmedṛśaṃ dharmyaṃ dvijena kṛtam acyuta
english: Ah, blessed indeed is this world, and fortunate are the men upon the earth, wherein such a righteous deed was wrought by a Brahmin, O unfallen one."

sanskrit: tathā yāntau tadā tāta tāv acyutayudhiṣṭhirau jagmatur yatra gāṅgeyaḥ śaratalpagataḥ prabhuḥ
english: As they journeyed on thus, O dear one, those two—the unfallen Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira—came to where the lordly son of Gaṅgā lay upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: tatas te dadṛśur bhīṣmaṃ śaraprastaraśāyinam svaraśmijālasaṃvītaṃ sāyaṃsūryam ivānalam
english: Then they beheld Bhīṣma lying upon his couch of arrows, wrapped about in the net of his own radiance, like the evening sun, like blazing fire.

sanskrit: upāsyamānaṃ munibhir devair iva śatakratum deśe paramadharmiṣṭhe nadīmoghavatīm anu
english: He was attended by sages as Indra of the hundred sacrifices is attended by the gods, in that most holy region beside the river Oghavatī.

sanskrit: dūrād eva tam ālokya kṛṣṇo rājā ca dharmarāṭ catvāraḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva te ca śāradvatādayaḥ
english: Beholding him from afar, Kṛṣṇa and the King of righteousness, and the four Pāṇḍavas, and those headed by the son of Śaradvat—

sanskrit: avaskandyātha vāhebhyaḥ saṃyamya pracalaṃ manaḥ ekīkṛtyendriyagrāmam upatasthur mahāmunīn
english: —alighting then from their mounts, restraining their restless minds and gathering together the host of their senses, they approached the great sages.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca govindaḥ sātyakis te ca kauravāḥ vyāsādīṃs tān ṛṣīn paścād gāṅgeyam upatasthire
english: And having paid homage to those sages headed by Vyāsa, Govinda, Sātyaki, and the Kauravas thereafter drew near to the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tapovṛddhiṃ tataḥ pṛṣṭvā gāṅgeyaṃ yadukauravāḥ parivārya tataḥ sarve niṣeduḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Then, having inquired after the increase of his austerities, the Yadus and the Kauravas, those bulls among men, all surrounded the son of Gaṅgā and sat down.

sanskrit: tato niśamya gāṅgeyaṃ śāmyamānam ivānalam kiṃ cid dīnamanā bhīṣmam iti hovāca keśavaḥ
english: Then, observing the son of Gaṅgā—like a fire slowly dying down—Keśava, his heart somewhat grieved, spoke thus to Bhīṣma:

sanskrit: kaccij jñānāni te rājan prasannāni yathā purā kaccid avyākulā caiva buddhis te vadatāṃ vara
english: "Are your faculties of knowledge, O king, clear as they were of old? And is your understanding undisturbed, O best of speakers?

sanskrit: śarābhighātaduḥkhāt te kaccid gātraṃ na dūyate mānasād api duḥkhād dhi śārīraṃ balavattaram
english: Does your body not burn with the pain of the arrows' wounds? For pain of the body is harder to bear even than pain of the mind.

sanskrit: varadānāt pituḥ kāmaṃ chandamṛtyur asi prabho śaṃtanor dharmaśīlasya na tv etac chamakāraṇam
english: By the boon granted by your father, you may die at your own will, O lord—for so the righteous-natured Śaṃtanu wished; yet this is no ground for tranquility of spirit."
